clues.text: This big town lies at the south foot of the Alborz range, where the hills meet a high flat plain. That plain fills the heart of the land to the south.
clues.narrowing: Puts the player at the foot of the Alborz range in West Asia.

source.quote: Tehran lies at the southern foot of the Alborz Mountains and the northern edge of the Iranian Central Plateau, giving the city a complex climate.

clues.text: Rain here falls mostly from late autumn to spring. The summer months are extremely dry and often pass with no rain at all.
clues.narrowing: Keeps a dry-summer city where rain belongs to the winter half of the year.

source.quote: The wet season spans from late autumn through early spring (roughly November to May), while the summer months (June to September) are extremely dry and often see no measurable rainfall.

clues.text: In 1786 a king of the Qajar line picked this town as his chief town. His pick made the town the seat of rule for the whole land.
clues.narrowing: Shrinks the list to capitals chosen by a Qajar king in 1786.

source.quote: Eventually, Qajar king Agha Mohammad Khan chose Tehran as the capital of Iran in 1786.

clues.text: The Azadi Tower stands tall in this town as a mark of the past. It went up in 1971, for 2,500 years since the Persian realm began.
clues.narrowing: Nearly decisive: one capital's landmark tower marks 2,500 years of the Persian Empire.

source.quote: Landmarks include the Azadi Tower, a memorial built in 1971 to mark the 2,500th anniversary of the Persian Empire

clues.text: Iran is run from this town, and the work of state is done here each day. More folk live here than in any town in the whole land.
clues.narrowing: Confirms it: capital and largest city of Iran.

source.quote: Tehran is the capital and largest city of Iran.

reveal.blurb: A Qajar king picked this city as his capital in 1786, after the land had already had fifty capitals before it. Today it is a giant city at the foot of the snowy Alborz Mountains, home to the white Azadi Tower. Tehran is the capital of Iran.
